issues.failure_explanation: Norm convergence F_eps -> F does not imply any convergence or equality of operator ranges. Ranges of compact operators are not closed, and 'lim Range' is undefined. The approximation g_eps -> g only shows that Range(L) lies in a closure. The statement itself is false under the relaxed hypothesis. A real continuous S with a null nodal set may change sign. Take D a ball centred at 0, S(y)=y_2 and x̂=e_1. Then u^∞(±e_1,ω)=0 for all ω, so F=0 and Range(F_#^{1/2})={0}, whereas Range(L)≠{0}. The same example makes Theorem A.1 give a false conclusion when it is applied to sign-indefinite T on D\Y_eps. Sources vanishing on a hyperplane orthogonal to x̂ also break the identity, because T_# is then not coercive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the strict condition |S|≥c_0>0 on D̄, which forces constant sign. RH then reduces to the cited identity of GGH2022. The claimed generalization (iii) must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The Picard characterization and every indicator built on it lack a valid basis under the paper's assumptions. Uniqueness from two opposite directions is even false: with S=y_2 the data at ±e_1 vanish for every t_0 and every symmetric D.
issues.title: Range identity under the relaxed condition |S|>0 a.e. is false, and its limit-of-ranges proof is invalid
issues.why_classification: The statement is false in the advertised regime. The only supported fix abandons the claimed weakening of the source assumption, and with it the generality of all downstream results.

Earlier approaches \cite{GS17,GGH2022} relied on test functions integrated over a small spatial domain.

issues.failure_explanation: For w in L^2(D) with D bounded, Lw(τ)=∫ e^{-iτ(c^{-1}s-t_0)} m(s) ds with m in L^1 of compact support. So Lw is entire and, by Riemann–Lebesgue, Lw(τ)→0 as |τ|→∞ on R. The test function e^{-iτ b} is entire with modulus 1. If the two agreed on (0,K), analytic continuation would make them agree on R, which is a contradiction. Hence φ_{z,η} is not in Range(L) for every z and η. The proof reaches the opposite conclusion only through the false Lemma lem4.1(ii).

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace pointwise test functions by ones that genuinely lie in Range(L), such as the domain-averaged test functions of GS17/GGH2022, and reprove the strip and time characterizations with them.
issues.overall_effect: Theoretically I_η=∞ everywhere, so W_η, h, I^{(x̂)} and I vanish identically. The claimed characterizations of the strips, of t_0 and of the Θ-hull, and the uniqueness proofs built on them, all fail. Innovation (ii) is unsupported.
issues.title: Point-defined test functions never lie in Range(L); the 'if' direction of the main characterization is false
issues.why_classification: The central theorem is false as stated and the advertised pointwise framework cannot be saved. A different test-function construction and new proofs are required.

issues.failure_explanation: Neither norm convergence of F_{N,#}^{1/2} nor density of exponentials yields equality of ranges in any sense, so (RIfN) is unsupported. The conclusion is in fact false. A nonzero exponential sum with distinct real a_m is almost periodic and does not decay. If it coincided with some Lw on (0,K), analytic continuation and Riemann–Lebesgue would give a contradiction. Hence Range(L_N)∩Range(L)={0} for all N, and membership in every Range(L_N) never implies membership in Range(L).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must delete part (ii) and supply an argument characterizing Range(L) that does not pass through limits of ranges of discretized operators.
issues.overall_effect: The only argument for the sufficiency part of Theorem lem3.4 collapses, and with it everything built on that theorem.
issues.title: Claimed equality Range(L)=lim Range(L_N) is false and its derivation is a non sequitur
issues.why_classification: The claim is false, not merely unproven. No comparable version supports the intended use, so the proof architecture of Section 3 must be replaced.

issues.failure_explanation: In R^3 the total volume of N balls of radius |D|/N is (4π/3)|D|^3/N^2, which tends to 0. Such balls cannot cover D, which has positive measure, for large N, so no sequence satisfies condition (ii). The equal-weight Riemann sums (|D|/N)ΣS(y_m)e^{...} would in any case need equidistribution, not a covering. The norm convergence F_N→F, used to obtain (RIfN), therefore rests on a nonexistent construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (ii) by requiring {y_m} to be uniformly distributed in D, keeping conditions (i) and (iii). Then F_N→F in norm follows from continuity of S.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence F_N→F feeding Lemma lem4.1(ii) is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Required covering of D by N balls of radius |D|/N is impossible
issues.why_classification: This is a local, standard replacement of the sampling condition with no further loss. Other defects of the lemma are reported separately.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $a(t)\in C([0,T])$ is a real-valued function, and $|a'(t)|<c, t\in [0,T]$.
The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.failure_explanation: At direction x̂, pulse j occupies the times t_j − c^{-1} x̂·(D_j+a(t_j)). The gap between consecutive pulses is Δt − x̂·Δa/c − width/c, and the motion term is ignored by the assumption. Take c=1, D_j a ball of diameter 1, Δt=1.5 and motion toward x̂ at speed 0.9. Then the gap is 1.5−1.35−1<0, so the pulses overlap although Assumption 1 holds. The single-pulse reduction used in the proof is therefore unjustified.

failure_location.quote: The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second assumption by a motion-aware condition, e.g. c(t_j−t_{j−1}) > |a(t_j)−a(t_{j−1})| + diam(D_j)/2 + diam(D_{j−1})/2 with D_j taken relative to the centres a(t_j). Alternatively, state the corollary only for already separated data u_j^∞.
issues.overall_effect: Recovering all t_j and D_j from measured total time-domain data is not supported. The intro's separability claim is false in general.
issues.title: Separability of pulses does not follow from Assumption 1 for a moving source
issues.why_classification: A stronger, motion-dependent hypothesis is needed, which narrows the scope. The single-pulse method itself is unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Eigenvectors of F diagonalize Re F and Im F, with eigenvalues |Re λ|+|Im λ| for F_#, only when F is normal. Here F=LTL^* with T a multiplication operator that does not commute with L^*L, and the Toeplitz matrix is generally non-normal. So the stated eigensystem of (F)_# is incorrect in general, and the discrete indicators (indicator5)-(indicator7) built from it compute the wrong quantity.

failure_location.quote: an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the eigen-decomposition of the Hermitian matrix |Re F|+|Im F| directly, as the paper's alternative suggests, and drop the derivation from the eigenpairs of F.
issues.overall_effect: Numerical indicators computed this way do not approximate the Picard series for F_#.
issues.title: Eigensystem of F_# wrongly derived from eigensystem of the non-normal matrix F
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local change in the numerical recipe that the paper already mentions. No theory or claimed guarantee changes.
